 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti

entities.text:
New India Assurance Company Limited vs Smt. K.
Kathalamma And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the award and decree dated 14.02.2008 in O.P.Nos.536 of 2001, 541 of 2001 and 542 of 2001 on the file of the VII Additional District Judge, Mahabubnagar, the Insurance Company filed this appeal.

2. Having heard Ms. I.Maamu Vani, learned counsel for the appellant insurance company and Mr.
K.Venkatesh Gupta, perused the entire material on record.

3. The claim petition was filed by the claimant seeking compensation of Rs.50,000/- for the death of the deceased in the accident which took place on 02.05.1998 and the Tribunal has granted the compensation as claimed.

4. The case of the claimant is that on 02.05.1998 at about 03.00 a.m. the deceased Neelamma, her husband and her son boarded the lorry to eke out their livelihood and at about 03.45 a.m. when the lorry was in the limits of Thatikonda Village, the driver of the lorry drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road culvert, due to which the lorry fell down, resulting in instantaneous death of neelamma, her husband and her son.
The claimant has filed an application under Section 140 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (for short 'the Act') seeking compensation under no fault liability.
The Court below has considered the evidence on record and granted compensation of Rs.50,000/-.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submitted that the passengers are gratuitous passengers and under the no fault liability also the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation.

She has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Jethu Rama and Others 1.
7.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Jethu Rama and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that though they are gratuitous passengers,
respondent Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation, as it is under the no fault liability.

He has relied upon the following judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court:
The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Smt. K. Kathalamma And Another on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191202755/

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the claimant submitted that this Act being a beneficial legislation and though they are gratuitous passengers, the Insurance Company should pay the amount and then recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
He has relied upon the judgments mentioned supra and the Judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Baljit Kaur 6.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Baljit Kaur 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the light of the law laid down in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Saju P.Paul 7,
the Tribunal has already ordered pay and recover and in the light of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Asha Rani 8 case, if at that point of time, if the same is reversed lot of hardship would be caused to the claimant therein.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Asha Rani
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In those facts and circumstances, the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that still the Insurance Company shall pay and recover.
In none of the judgments, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that though there is violation of conditions of the policy, still the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation.
However, exercising the discretion under Section 142 of the Act, the Hon'ble Apex Court has ordered the same.

2022 Law Suit(TS) 257 (2004) 2 SCC 1 : 2004 SCC (Cri) 370 (2013) 2 SCC 41 (2003) 2 SCC 223 4 LK,J MACMA_1538_2009 9. In the light of the settled decision in Asha Rani's case (cited 8 supra) and thereafter in Baljit Kaur's case (cited 6 supra), in case of gratuitous passengers, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation and it is the owner alone who is liable to pay the compensation.
10. Hence, the appeal of the Insurance Company is allowed holding that the owner of the vehicle alone is liable to pay the compensation.

The accident is of the year 1998 and the claimant has withdrawn certain amounts as per the interim order, balancing the interest of both the parties the Insurance Company shall not recover the money already deposited from the claimant.
However, the Insurance Company is at liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
